milestone.title: raul TUI mouse support — click and double-click across all lanes (Milestones, Backlog, Ideas, Path, Overview, Settings, Autopilot)

intent.outcome: Every raul lane supports mouse interaction consistent with keyboard: click on a row selects it; double-click on a row opens its detail; scroll-wheel scrolls the list (Milestones queue, Backlog list, Ideas list, Path swimlanes, Overview cards, Autopilot queue). On touch-screen devices (e.g. running raul over a phone SSH session) the ergonomics are usable: long-press maps to double-click; vertical swipe maps to scroll-wheel.

problem.description: Today most raul lanes are keyboard-only. Mouse clicks fall through to the underlying terminal; wheel events do nothing. Specifically: (a) Milestones tab: click selects a row, but double-click does not open the milestone detail; (b) Backlog and Ideas tabs: clicking an item does not even select it; (c) Path swimlanes, Overview cards, Settings rows have partial coverage from earlier milestones; (d) Autopilot lane (M216) is fully keyboard-only. On a phone or a tablet connected via SSH/Screen, keyboard input is painful — taps are the natural mode. The fix is a TUI-wide mouse-handler surface wired into each lane's render dispatcher; the harness-level event loop already delivers mouse events via ratatui, so this is a layer-up exercise, not new infrastructure.

in_scope: Click-to-select on rows in Milestones, Backlog, Ideas, Path, Overview, Settings, Autopilot. Currently partial; extend to all lanes with consistent semantics (clicking a row sets the active index; Esc clears it).
Double-click on a row to open detail view: Milestones → milestone detail; Backlog → entry detail; Ideas → idea detail; Path → milestone detail; Autopilot → per-milestone detail panel (M216 AC-05).
Scroll-wheel support on lists: Milestones backlog, Backlog list, Ideas list, Path swimlanes, Overview cards, Settings rows, Autopilot pane rows + queue.
Touch-screen compatibility: long-press (200–400ms hold) maps to double-click; vertical swipe maps to wheel events. Tested on Termux/iSH SSH sessions if available, otherwise documented.
Backwards compatibility: keyboard input remains the canonical path; mouse support is additive and never overrides keyboard shortcuts.
Per-lane wiring tests + a TUI-wide integration test that drives a click + double-click sequence against `crates/raul/tests/suite_mouse_lanes.rs`.
out_of_scope: Drag-to-reorder (Milestones / Backlog priority reordering via drag is a separate interaction; current keyboard-based reorder is unchanged).
Right-click context menus (a future affordance; not needed now).
Hover tooltips in the autopilot lane's per-pane status rows (M216 currently has no hover; mouse hover would need a different time-tracking mechanism).
Configuring mouse sensitivity or long-press duration (sensible defaults; configurability can land later via the keybinds config system).
Drag-and-drop for the per-milestone queue (key-based reordering stays).

design_decisions.choice: A single `crates/raul/src/tui/mouse.rs` module owns the click/double-click/scroll mapping. Each lane's app.rs calls into it once per render cycle.
design_decisions.rationale: Centralizes long-press detection and double-click debouncing; one place to test the time thresholds.

design_decisions.choice: Long-press threshold default 250ms; configurable via a constant (not via the keybinds.toml — left for a future milestone if anyone needs it).
design_decisions.rationale: Matches Android's long-press default and is a single tunable; keybinds config (M222) doesn't need to grow for this.

design_decisions.choice: `RAUL_NO_MOUSE=1` env var bypasses the mouse handler at startup. Documentation calls this out for users on systems where mouse events confuse the terminal emulator.
design_decisions.rationale: Some terminals forward spurious mouse events; escape hatch keeps the keyboard path pristine.

steps.action: Add `crates/raul/src/tui/mouse.rs`: a small module that exposes `try_handle_mouse(app, mouse_event) -> Consumed` and helpers `try_click`, `try_double_click`, `try_scroll`. Each lane's app.rs calls these once per render cycle.
